stem: Bile, an alkaline fluid that emulsifies dietary lipids, is produced by which of the following cell types?

options.label: A
options.misconception: None; hepatocytes synthesize and export bile to the duodenum.
options.explanation: The digestive role of the liver is to produce bile and export it to the duodenum; hepatocytes in the liver lobules are the source.

options.label: B
options.misconception: The storage organ is being cast as the producer.
options.explanation: The gallbladder stores, concentrates, and releases bile made by the liver; it does not synthesize bile.

options.label: C
options.misconception: A digestive enzyme source is being confused with bile production.
options.explanation: Pancreatic acini secrete enzyme-rich juice; bile is a hepatic product.

options.label: D
options.text: Goblet cells of the duodenal mucosa
options.misconception: A mucus-secreting cell is being assigned bile synthesis.
options.explanation: Goblet cells secrete protective mucus; bile arrives from the liver via the biliary tree.

options.label: E
options.text: Chief cells of the gastric mucosa
options.misconception: A gastric protease source is being confused with hepatic bile.
options.explanation: Chief cells secrete pepsinogen; bile is produced only by hepatocytes.

context: Learning objective: identify the bile source. Hepatocytes produce bile — an alkaline lipid-emulsifying solution — and export it to the duodenum; the gallbladder only stores and concentrates it.
